transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been troubling you and what brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t really stop thinking about how the left side of my face looks. Like my nose and jaw seem crooked to me, especially in ID photos or when I see myself on the camera for online classes.

People tell me they don’t really notice anything, but I still feel like everyone in the CNC lab sees it right away, before they notice anything I’m doing or the work I’m turning in. It’s been bothering me a lot.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking photos, or comparing sides of your face, because of your concern about how your face looks?

Yeah. I check it a lot, especially before I leave for school. I’ll get stuck in the bathroom mirror, then use my phone camera to look at it from different angles.

I’ll mess with my hair or change shirts because I feel like some clothes make the crookedness stand out more. I also ask my mom if it looks weird, sometimes more than once. It can take so long that I miss lab, or I get there already exhausted and can’t really focus.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms align more closely with Body dysmorphic disorder (F45.22) given the preoccupation with perceived facial asymmetry leading to repetitive behaviors and functional impairment. Body image distortion not otherwise specified (F44.5) remains as a related differential, but the clinical picture is more consistent with F45.22. Major depressive disorder (F32.9) and Social anxiety disorder (F40.00) are less likely given the specific focus on appearance rather than general depressive or social anxiety symptoms.

candidates: F32.9 - Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
F44.5 - Body image distortion not otherwise specified
